title: Short Stuff: How Often Do You Need To Change Your Oil?
summary: Short Stuff episode on how often to change car oil. Josh and Chuck discuss the no-appointment quick-lube shops and why they recommend a regular mechanic, then explain that the old three-thousand-mile or three-month oil change rule is outdated for newer cars. They cover the dashboard oil life indicator light versus the low-oil warning light (stop driving immediately), and why the sticker in the window should be ignored. Owner's manuals list a normal and a severe schedule; severe driving means short trips and stop-and-go traffic, which is harder on the engine because water condensation builds up unless the engine runs long enough (roughly ten-plus miles at highway speed) to burn it off. They discuss synthetic versus conventional oil, including its benefits and environmental tradeoffs, and briefly mention canola-based oil. The closing advice is to follow the indicator light, consult the owner's manual, and change oil at least every six months if you drive short trips.
topics: three thousand mile oil change myth

segments.title: Opening banter and quick-lube shops
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck open the episode, joke about Josh being overdue for an oil change, and discuss avoiding no-appointment quick-lube shops in favor of a regular mechanic.

segments.title: Oil life light versus low oil warning
segments.summary: Chuck explains the oil life indicator light and the separate low-oil light, which means stop driving as soon as possible. They discuss how running out of oil can destroy an engine.

segments.title: Why the three-thousand-mile rule is outdated
segments.summary: The hosts say the old three-thousand-mile or three-month guideline no longer applies to newer cars, since the indicator system monitors oil condition. They say the window sticker is a sales gimmick and to check the owner's manual, which lists a normal and a severe schedule.
topics: three thousand mile oil change myth

segments.title: Normal versus severe driving and condensation
segments.summary: Severe driving means short trips and stop-and-go traffic. Water condensation can build up in oil, and highway driving of more than about ten miles burns it off, so short-trip drivers should use the shorter interval.

segments.title: Synthetic oil, environment, and canola oil
segments.summary: The hosts compare synthetic and conventional oil, noting synthetics last longer and perform better but cost more. They discuss environmental effects of fewer oil changes and mention canola-based engine oil as an experimental alternative.

segments.title: Recap and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh recaps: follow the oil life light, consult the owner's manual, ignore the sticker, and change oil about every six months if driving short trips. The show closes with an email invitation.
